title: BBD descent for derived objects with vanishing negative self extensions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal B$ be a set of open subsets covering $X$ such that each intersection $U\cap V$ with $U,V\in\mathcal B$ is a union of elements of $\mathcal B$ contained in that intersection. For every $U\in\mathcal B$ suppose $K_U\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ is given [def-pc-derived-category], and for every inclusion $V\subset U$ in $\mathcal B$ suppose an isomorphism $\rho_V^U:K_U|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}K_V$ is given. Assume $\rho_U^U=1$ and $\rho_W^U=\rho_W^V\circ(\rho_V^U|_W)$ for $W\subset V\subset U$. Assume also that $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K_U,K_U[i])=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every integer $i<0$. Then there exist $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and isomorphisms $\rho_U:K|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}K_U$ with $\rho_V^U\circ(\rho_U|_V)=\rho_V$ for every inclusion $V\subset U$ in $\mathcal B$. The pair $(K,(\rho_U))$ is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with all these identifications. There is no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $X$.

proof.text: For any union $O$ of members of $\mathcal B$, write $\mathcal B_O=\{U\in\mathcal B:U\subset O\}$. It covers $O$ and has the same intersection-refinement property. Call $(F,(s_U))$ a solution on $O$ when $s_U:F|_U\cong K_U$ and $\rho_V^U(s_U|_V)=s_V$. For two such solutions $(F,s)$ and $(F',s')$, their local cross negative Hom groups vanish because both restrictions are isomorphic to $K_U$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on $O$ to the inclusion-compatible family $(s'_U)^{-1}s_U$. It gives one global map $a:F\to F'$. Apply it again to the inverse family to obtain $b:F'\to F$; injectivity on Hom makes $ba=1$ and $ab=1$, and proves uniqueness of $a$ among all compatible maps. The vanishing clause of the same lemma, with $M=N=F$, gives $\operatorname{Hom}(F,F[i])=0$ for $i<0$. These arguments also apply to any intersection-refining subfamily covering $O$.

source.place: Tags 0D66, 0D68 and 0D69: uniqueness, negative Ext, and restriction to subfamilies

proof.text: Well-order $\mathcal B=(U_\xi)_{\xi<\kappa}$ and put $W_\alpha=\bigcup_{\xi<\alpha}U_\xi$ for $\alpha\le\kappa$. We construct by transfinite recursion a solution $(F_\alpha,s_{\alpha,U})$ on each $W_\alpha$. By Step 1 every such object has negative self Hom vanishing. For $\beta<\alpha$, Step 1 applied on $W_\beta$ gives the unique comparison $r_\beta^\alpha:F_\alpha|_{W_\beta}\cong F_\beta$ satisfying $s_{\beta,U}(r_\beta^\alpha|_U)=s_{\alpha,U}$. These comparisons compose because both composites satisfy this displayed equation for every $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\gamma}$, and the Hom bijection makes them equal. At stage zero take the zero complex on the empty scheme; all its module sheaves and maps are zero, so it is a solution even if the empty open belongs to $\mathcal B$.

At a successor, the supplied object $K_{U_\alpha}$ is a solution on $U_\alpha$ with maps $\rho_V^{U_\alpha}$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-binary-extension] to this solution and the solution on $W_\alpha$. Its conclusion gives a solution on $W_{\alpha+1}$ with every original-family identification, including opens crossing the two pieces. Step 1 gives negative self Hom and all earlier comparisons.

source.place: Tags 0D69 (cohomology-remark-uniqueness), 0D6A (cohomology-lemma-solution-in-finite-case), and 0D6C (cohomology-theorem-glueing-bbd-general), overlap comparisons and successor step.

proof.text: At a nonzero limit $\lambda\le\kappa$, apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-limit-extension] to the earlier solutions and their comparisons from Step 2. The opens are increasing, continuous, and start with $\varnothing$; Step 1 gives negative self Hom, and Step 2 gives the comparison cocycle and preservation of all structure maps. The conclusion supplies the complete solution on $W_\lambda$ and comparisons preserving every earlier identification. Step 1 again supplies its negative self Hom.

source.place: Tags 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union) and 0D6C (cohomology-theorem-glueing-bbd-general), limit step and final compatibility bookkeeping.

proof.text: This completes the recursion. Since $W_\kappa=X$, take $K=F_\kappa$ and $\rho_U=s_{\kappa,U}$. Step 1 proves uniqueness by the Hom bijection [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue]. The well-order is on the given set $\mathcal B$; no finite subcover or quasi-compactness was used.
